round1.evidence: No sources found for a 'Central Square' beach in Kefalonia; name likely informal/local.
Sources describe Porto Atheras as a sheltered sandy family beach but none explicitly mention sunbeds/umbrellas or a beach bar.
1001beach describes Vrachinari (end of Vatsa Bay) as a quiet cozy sandy beach with fenced turtle nests; no mention of sunbeds or a bar.
Search summaries vaguely claim 'sunbeds and umbrellas provided' but no specific source page for this small pebble beach at Sami confirms it; guide page 404s.
Conflicting sources for Agia Varvara (Katelios): one says sunbeds, umbrellas and playground; another says no beach bar or sunbeds to protect the turtle-nesting environment.
Sources cover Nikiana's main beach (partly organized) but nothing specifically distinguishes the southern stretch.
No specific source found for Ampelakia on Meganisi (name collides with Peloponnese beaches); island guides say only Fanari beach is fully organized on Meganisi.
ecozante on Xigia 'dipla' (the small adjacent cove): 'usually few umbrellas and loungers, so if you want shade it's better to bring your own' — sparse/seasonal, main Xigia has the canteen.
No source clearly describing Madrakia beach on Zakynthos was found (searches returned Marathias and unrelated beaches).
Vourderi (Vasilikos) pages found describe location/history only; no explicit mention of sunbeds, umbrellas or a beach bar.
Official ithaca.gr lists Dexa as 'Pebbles, canteen' only — a canteen but no mention of sunbeds/umbrellas or a bar; natural shade from olive trees.
No source specific to Katsouni on Psara found; results collide with Katsouni beaches on Rhodes and Anafi.
No specific source found for Fytema; Ikaria organized-beach lists (Mesakti, Livadi, Kampos, Gialiskari) do not include it.
No source specific to Avlaki on Lesvos found; name collides with Avlaki in Attica and Corfu.
A taverna ("Drota", since 2017) sits on the beach, but no source states sunbeds/umbrellas; described as a quiet natural pebble beach.
Kagia near Skala Sikamnias has a fish taverna at the beach but is described as a natural, undeveloped pebble beach; no explicit sunbed/organization statement found.
Visit Lesvos describes Mikri/Megali Tsichranta as small idyllic coves ideal for isolation and quiet swimming; no facilities mentioned but no explicit 'unorganized' statement.
Conflicting: samosin.gr says Balos (SW Samos) is not organized with tavernas by the road, while the bathing water profile says a section has umbrellas/loungers.
Searches only return the main Lemonakia beach (organized); could not disambiguate a distinct 'Mikra Lemonakia' cove, so no beach-specific evidence.
All 'Bouka organized' evidence refers to Bouka in Messinia (Messiniakos Gulf), not the Argolida beach; no Argolida-specific source found.
Conflicting: one source says only a few straw umbrellas and no loungers, another (pocket-guide) calls it organized with sunbeds, umbrellas and a cafe snack bar.

No source clearly describing this specific beach was found; the only search hit described Alepochori beach 'across from the Alkyonides' (a different beach), so evidence cannot be attributed to this location.

Sources conflict: described as 'ανοργάνωτη, ωστόσο υπάρχει ένα ταβερνάκι ακριβώς δίπλα', while another notes the fish taverna 'απλώνει μερικές ομπρέλες και ξαπλώστρες πάνω στην ακροθαλασσιά' — a few taverna sunbeds, not a fully organized beach.
Only a Facebook page exists; no source describing facilities was found.
Only an aggregator entry describing it as 'a small pebbly beach' ~0.23km long, with no facility information; no sunbed/bar evidence found.

Limani at Elia (Monemvasia municipality): a narrow 4-5m sand strip; 'οι λουόμενοι προτιμούν να φιλοξενούνται στον λιμενοβραχίονα... στον οποίο υπάρχουν ξαπλώστρες' and it is framed by cafe-restaurants — sunbeds on the jetty, not clearly an organized beach.
